import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a professional style for the plot
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between megapixels and price,
# with different sensor types highlighted by color.
# This helps to see if certain sensor types are associated with higher megapixels or price points.
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='weight_grams', # Use weight to add another dimension of insight
    sizes=(50, 500), # Range for point sizes
    palette='viridis', # A perceptually uniform colormap
    alpha=0.7, # Transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    edgecolor='w', # White edge around points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type and Weight', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data points
# The 'hue' legend (Sensor Type) and 'size' legend (Weight) are handled automatically by seaborn
plt.legend(title='Camera Characteristics', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add grid for better readability of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust plot layout to prevent elements from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for legend outside

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
